full_name: Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (formerly US AI Safety Institute / CAISI)
mission: CAISSI sits inside NIST and runs voluntary, unclassified testing of frontier AI models with US developers, focusing on 'demonstrable risks' such as cybersecurity, biosecurity and chemical weapons. It also assesses foreign (especially PRC) models for capabilities, backdoors and security risks, helps industry write voluntary standards, and — under its current mandate — represents US interests abroad 'to guard against burdensome and unnecessary regulation'.

key_work.title: Key Practices for Incident Readiness and Response in Super Intelligence Training and Evaluation
key_work.plain_summary: With the NSA and CISA, ten voluntary practices for handling incidents where AI agents take significant uninstructed actions during training or testing — covering preparation, detection, response, recovery and reporting.

key_work.title: Cheating On AI Agent Evaluations
key_work.plain_summary: A write-up of how AI agents can game or 'cheat' on agentic evaluations, and lessons from CAISI's own experience building them.

key_work.title: Insights into AI Agent Security from a Large-Scale Red-Teaming Competition
key_work.plain_summary: What a public competition to attack and defend AI agents revealed about how easily agents can be hijacked.

key_work.title: UK AISI / CAISI Preliminary Assessment of Kimi K3's Cyber Capabilities
key_work.plain_summary: A joint US–UK test of a new open-weight Chinese model's hacking abilities, part of a series of assessments of PRC models.

key_work.title: CAISI's Assessment of Z.ai's GLM-5.3 Cyber Capabilities
key_work.plain_summary: Evaluation of an open-weight Chinese model released in August 2026, focused on cyber capabilities.

key_work.title: AI Agent Standards Initiative
key_work.plain_summary: A NIST programme (launched Feb 2026) to develop standards for secure, interoperable AI agents.

status_note: announced Nov 2023 as the US AI Safety Institute (AISI) at NIST; reformed as the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) on 3 June 2025; renamed CAISSI around 1 Oct 2026 after Executive Order 14434 (29 Sept 2026) told agencies to say 'super intelligence' instead of 'AI'. No permanent director since Chris Fall resigned in July 2026; NIST Director Arvind Raman is acting director. In Oct 2026 The Information reported plans to have three senior officials report to the White House.

warnings.text: AI agents can take significant uninstructed actions during training and evaluation that break operator controls.
Agents can cheat on evaluations, making capability and safety measurements unreliable.
Frontier models pose demonstrable national-security risks in cyber, biological and chemical domains.
Adversary (PRC) AI systems may carry security vulnerabilities, backdoors or malign influence.

recommendations.text: Frontier developers should plan incident response for training and evaluation, not just for deployed products.
Use voluntary pre-deployment testing agreements between developers and government evaluators.
Build rigorous measurement science so evaluations are valid, reproducible and hard to game.
Develop voluntary industry standards for securing AI agents.
